tldr: On the scalar Bernoulli observational class with exactly uniform covariates, the whole-curve integrated squared-error minimax risk is \(R_n\asymp n^{-q}\), including equality without a logarithm. A total fine-bin pair covariance ratio attains this rate, and a simultaneous target hypercube supplies the same-class all-estimator converse. Revealing the propensity on that identical class gives \(R_n^e\asymp n^{-q_o}\), with a strict unknown-propensity penalty below the nuisance elbow. For \(\gamma\ge\beta\), subclass inclusion also gives \(R_n^{\mathrm{KBRW},L^2(Q_X)}\ge R_n\ge cn^{-q}\) in the scalar Conditions-1--4 model with a fixed density upper envelope and no density lower bound. This broader design-weighted result is a lower corollary; matching attainment remains exact-uniform. The exponent is credited to the published pointwise theory and its global prediction; the new work is global assembly, whole-curve variance control and the exact-class oracle comparison.
